name: 2+ doors
description: The Narrator has an integer array $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$, but he will only tell you the size $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ statements, each of them being three integers $$$i, j, x$$$, which means that $$$a_i \mid a_j = x$$$, where $$$|$$$ denotes the bitwise OR operation . Find the lexicographically smallest array $$$a$$$ that satisfies all the statements. An array $$$a$$$ is lexicographically smaller than an array $$$b$$$ of the same length if and only if the following holds: in the first position where $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ differ, the array $$$a$$$ has a smaller element than the corresponding element in $$$b$$$.
input_specification: In the first line you are given with two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$, $$$0 \le q \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$). In the next $$$q$$$ lines you are given with three integers $$$i$$$, $$$j$$$, and $$$x$$$ ($$$1 \le i, j \le n$$$, $$$0 \le x \lt 2^{30}$$$) — the statements. It is guaranteed that all $$$q$$$ statements hold for at least one array.
output_specification: On a single line print $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \lt 2^{30}$$$) — array $$$a$$$.
approach_summary: Convert boolean constraints to implication edges (¬A => B, ¬B => A). Compute SCCs using Tarjan's; a valid assignment exists iff no variable shares an SCC with its negation.
